BOUNDS AN EARLIER FINDING RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. Viewport#nonce-attribute concluded with "any attributes('x') assertion on a prop-path binding is suspect; sweep for them" — the sweep is now done and the hazard is ONE attribute, not a class. Counted every .attributes('…') assertion in the 97 jsdom originals: 421 of them over 41 distinct names. Confirmed the mechanism from source rather than memory: shouldSetAsProp ends in `return key in el` tested against the EXACT lowercase key (@vue/runtime-dom@3.5.17/dist/runtime-dom.cjs.js:763), after a short deny-list; patchDOMProp (L564) then assigns el[key] = value. Probed every plausibly-IDL name in BOTH environments (jsdom 20.0.3 in node, Chromium via playwright 1.62.1, modelling patchDOMProp directly). Result: disabled/required reflect '' on both; type/dir/placeholder/id/style reflect identically; NONCE IS THE ONLY TEST-VISIBLE DIVERGENCE (jsdom 'abc123', Chromium null). The reason the blast radius is small is mechanical — `key in el` needs the exact spelling, and the IDL names are tabIndex/readOnly/inputMode/ariaLabel/ariaValueNow, none of which match the hyphenated or lowercase attribute, so they take setAttribute. That exempts every aria-* (~150 assertions) and every data-* (data-state alone is 92). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: do NOT treat attributes('x') as a review flag on the remaining files; the 33 assertions on IDL-shaped names are all safe bar nonce. NEW NUANCE: role shows `key in el` is ITSELF environment-dependent — 'role' in div is false under jsdom 20 and true in Chromium (ARIA reflection, Element.role) — so Vue takes DIFFERENT CODE PATHS in the two environments for the same binding. Invisible here only because Chromium's role setter reflects.

RE-VERDICTS A CLAIM IN AN EARLIER PORT'S OWN FINDING, AND THE ERROR IS INSTRUCTIVE. AlertDialog's row called container-vs-document scoping "THE ONE TRANSLATION THAT IS NOT IN THE TABLE AND WOULD SILENTLY BREAK A PORT", and its port carries a comment saying screen.getBy* "would find nothing once the dialog is open". Teleport's port contradicted it; settled by probe against the disputed fixture itself (_AlertDialog.vue, dialog open, probe file written, run, deleted): content's parentElement is BODY and screen.container.contains(content) is FALSE — so the content really is portalled out — yet screen.getByRole('alertdialog') returns 1 and it is the SAME NODE page.getByRole returns (identity-checked, not just count-checked); screen.locator.getByRole returns 0. Independently corroborated from source: vitest-browser-vue@2.1.0 dist/pure-epEwB8Ps.js L20 baseElement = customBaseElement || customContainer || document.body, L45 ...getElementLocatorSelectors(baseElement), L34 locator: page.elementLocator(container). So the helpers are DOCUMENT-scoped and only screen.locator/screen.container are container-scoped. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE FILE: the wrong rule was about to be inherited by the eight T3 overlays, and it fails in the direction that looks like diligence — an agent handed it "fixes" queries that already work. THE REAL HAZARD IS THE INVERSE ONE, which the wrong rule hid: because the helpers are document-scoped, screen.getBy* also sees OTHER renders (measured: two render() calls in one test, the first screen's getByText matches the second component). No completed port is wrong — page.getBy* is correct, just not required — so nothing was changed but the misleading comment. LESSON FOR THE APPARATUS: a finding written from a real symptom can still name the wrong cause, and this one survived a batch because it was plausible and its port was green. Findings are evidence, not verdicts; the ones that generalise furthest deserve a second measurement before the next batch inherits them.

10/10 tests, 14/14 assertions, port:checklist --complete and port:parity --complete clean, 1 quarantined (#animated-content-is-jsdom-only). The original installs no stubs, so nothing is deleted - but this is the T2 file where the environment, not the harness, earns the gain. GAINED is exactly the animation path: usePresence.ts L73-L76 (isAnimating / ANIMATION_OUT / leave) and L125+L127 (handleAnimationStart, which needs a real animationstart event jsdom never fires). Four branches flip too, from the istanbul branch map: L74 if [0,0] jsdom -> [1,0] browser and its && [0,0] -> [1,1]; L125 if [0,0] -> [2,0]; L53 if [4,0] -> [5,2] (browser learns that opening WITH an animation must not dispatch after-enter early); L56 else-if [6,0] -> [11,1]; L57 3-clause || [6,0,0] -> [12,1,1] (jsdom never evaluates clauses 2 and 3 because clause 1 is always true); L101 direction cond [1,0] -> [1,1]. The sharpest single number is L183 getAnimationName: the `|| 'none'` fallback is taken 15/15 times under jsdom and 0/26 in Chromium - jsdom's getComputedStyle().animationName is the empty string for every element that has ever existed, so under jsdom getAnimationName is a constant function. vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'getComputedStyle') ports unchanged (Window.prototype method, spyOn shadows it with an own property on the global, usePresence calls it unqualified). Three deviations, each with its own row: #state-accumulation, #synthetic-animation-event, #animated-content-is-jsdom-only.

QUARANTINED via it.fails - reported, not fixed, and the "bug" is in the test, not the library. `given a Presence with animated content` injects its own <style> with real @keyframes and asserts that after closing, "should not show content". In Chromium the keyframes actually run: data-state flips to closed, animation-name becomes fadeOut, usePresence reads the change, dispatches ANIMATION_OUT and holds the node mounted - which is the component's entire reason to exist. Measured through the cycle with a probe: after open+nextTick animationName=fadeIn; after close+nextTick animationName=fadeOut and the node is still mounted; still mounted at +500ms; gone at +2500ms, i.e. after the real animationend. Verified the port fails on the assertion and not on an error (flipped it.fails to it once: "expected '<div><button> toggle </button><div cl...' not to contain 'Content'", with the received HTML showing data-state="closed"). So the jsdom test asserts the OPPOSITE of correct browser behaviour and passes only because jsdom cannot run CSS animations. Do NOT "fix" this by shortening the animation or awaiting animationend - that would make the describe name a lie in the other direction. The honest resolution is to rewrite the block around the animation lifecycle, which the verbatim-name rule forbids here.

MUTATION, and the cleanest jsdom-vs-browser divergence found in T2 so far. Replaced usePresence.ts:183 with `return node ? (getComputedStyle(node), 'none') : 'none'` - the component still calls getComputedStyle (so the spy test is unaffected) but never looks at animation-name again, i.e. Presence loses the whole feature it exists for. Result: jsdom 10/10 STILL PASS. The browser port detects it - the quarantined it.fails goes green and therefore reports as failed, which is the .fails mechanism working as designed. So all 10 jsdom tests together cannot distinguish the real usePresence from one that ignores animations entirely, and three of those tests are named "given a Presence with animated content". Corollary for the other 3 files whose fixtures animate: a jsdom test can never fail an animation regression in this library.

AUDIT OF A HARNESS DECISION, requested because usePresence is the code that decision cites. tailwind.browser.config.js says it omits the keyframes/animation theme and tailwindcss-animate so "animate-* classes compile to nothing", justified by "Reka's usePresence already handles animation-name: none". VERDICT: the decision is SOUND, its stated rationale is TRUE, and one sentence of the comment is FALSE. (1) True: measured animationName=none, duration=0s for animate-slideUp, animate-fadeOut, animate-slideDownAndFade and the variant form data-[state=closed]:animate-slideUp, and usePresence then takes the instant-unmount branch exactly as under jsdom - ported tests keep behaving the same. (2) False: `animate-*` does NOT universally compile to nothing. The config uses theme.extend, so Tailwind's DEFAULT animation theme survives - animate-spin measured animationName=spin, duration=1s, infinite, and `spin` is the one @keyframes rule in the compiled CSS. animate-pulse/bounce/ping are absent only because no fixture references them (JIT content scan), not because the theme dropped them. The two animate-spin users are TreeAsync.story.vue and ComboboxAsyncOptions.story.vue - both *.story.vue, neither mounted by a test - so nothing is affected today, but an infinitely spinning element is exactly what Playwright's actionability stability check waits forever on, so the next person must not trust the comment. (3) The real cost: 3 fixtures that tests DO mount carry data-[state=closed]:animate-* on Presence-controlled nodes - _Accordion.vue (slideUp), _Toast.vue (hide/swipeOut), _NavigationMenu.vue (scaleOut/fadeOut). Measured on _Accordion in the browser project: animationName=none in both open and closed states, so the exit-animation path stays dead for those ports too. (4) But the shim is not throwing the capability away, and that is the decisive point: this file proves a locally injected <style> drives the full ANIMATION_OUT -> animationstart -> animationend -> unmount cycle in Chromium and is worth +6 lines and 4 branches. Enabling the animations globally instead would be actively harmful - every overlay port would wait out a real exit animation before its "content is gone" assertion, and dozens of assertions would change meaning at once. RECOMMENDATION: keep the shim as is, fix the comment's "compile to nothing" claim, and opt in per test where the animation IS the subject.

STRUCTURAL DEVIATION, and the original is order-dependent. Three of the four describes mount ONCE in the describe body and let open-state accumulate across tests: `after clicking trigger again` has no hook of its own, so its second click comes from the PARENT beforeEach re-running against a wrapper still open from the previous test. render auto-unmounts, so the port mounts per test and gives each "again" block a beforeEach that clicks a second time - same two clicks, same names, and the names become true by construction instead of by test ordering. The original's version is fragile, measured rather than argued: `vitest run --project=unit src/Presence/Presence.test.ts -t "should not show content"` FAILS 2 of 4 matched tests (the two "again" ones, both "expected ... not to contain 'Content'"), because skipping the sibling test removes one of the two clicks. The same filter against the port passes 3 + 1 expected fail. So the jsdom file cannot be run with -t, .only, or a shuffled sequence, and that fragility is invisible in a full-file run. The harness earns this one, not the browser - a jsdom file that mounted in beforeEach would be equally stable.

A BLOCK NO TEST IN EITHER SUITE EXECUTES, specified per branch from the istanbul map rather than by reading. usePresence.ts L106-L118 is the anti-flash handler: on the last animationend of an exit, it pins animationFillMode to "forwards" and schedules a setTimeout to put the old value back ("Doing this any sooner than setTimeout still causes a flash"). Counts, jsdom and browser identical: L106 if [0,0], L114 if [0,0], the setTimeout callback (fn at L113) 0 calls, L145 `if (timeoutId !== undefined)` [0,4] jsdom / [0,10] browser and L169 the same - so timeoutId is never assigned and the clearTimeout on both teardown paths never runs. L102 `if (isCurrentAnimation)` is [0,1] jsdom / [0,2] browser: never true even in the port. The reason is specific and fixable: the port's animated block reads immediately after the click and the test ends, so cleanup unmounts before the 2s fadeOut can finish. A probe that waits 2500ms DOES reach it (content unmounts, which can only happen via L102-L104 because animation-name is fadeOut, not none). So unlike the jsdom side this is reachable in browser mode - nothing here is a browser limitation, it is simply untested. Not fixed: an added test would be INVENTED and the quarantined test's body must stay unchanged.

A MOCK THE BROWSER MAKES UNNECESSARY, small but exactly the shape the thesis predicts. The original fakes an animation event with `new Event('animationend', { bubbles: true })` plus `Object.defineProperty(event, 'animationName', { value: 'child-animation' })`. Chromium has the real constructor, so the port uses `new AnimationEvent('animationend', { bubbles: true, animationName: 'child-animation' })` - same two dispatches, same two assertions, one fewer piece of fakery. The test itself is NOT a jsdom artifact and needed no other change: mutation-verified in both environments by deleting the `if (event.target !== node.value) return` guard at usePresence.ts:94, which turns exactly this test red under jsdom AND in the browser. It is the one test in the file that both environments can genuinely fail. vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'getComputedStyle') also ports unchanged - flagged in PORT-INVENTORY as `spyOn`, and confirmed to be a flag and not a hazard.

TWO TESTS QUARANTINED under it.fails, both asserting getAttribute('hidden') === '' on an unmountOnHide:false content: `should have hidden attribute` and the nested `should close the content`. CollapsibleContent.vue:109 binds :hidden to the STRING 'until-found' when unmountOnHide is false. Vue writes it as a DOM property, not an attribute (shouldSetAsProp ends in `key in el`, and 'hidden' in HTMLElement is true in both environments). jsdom 26.1.0 implements hidden as a plain BOOLEAN reflected IDL attribute, so el.hidden = 'until-found' coerces to true and getAttribute('hidden') reflects back '' (probed directly in node: attribute "", prop true, typeof boolean). Chromium implements the spec union (boolean or unrestricted double or DOMString) and reflects verbatim (probed in the port: attribute "until-found", prop "until-found", typeof string). THE COMPONENT IS CORRECT AND THE TEST WAS TESTING JSDOM — the original even says so, in a comment above the assertion: "`jsdom` doesn't render hidden attribute correctly / it should be `until-found`". Assertions left exactly as strong as they were IN THE SOURCE TEXT — but see #quarantine-swallows-siblings, because that is NOT the same as leaving them as strong in EFFECT: the nested `should close the content` carries three assertions and only this one throws, so under it.fails the other two stopped discriminating entirely. That was corrected by moving them into the block's beforeEach, not by changing this quarantine. it.fails still absorbs the hidden failure and turns red the day jsdom or the component changes. THIS BOUNDS attributes-sweep#nonce-does-not-generalise, which concluded nonce was the only test-visible IDL divergence in 421 assertions. It is the second, and the sweep could not have found it: the sweep probed names, and this divergence depends on the bound VALUE. patchDOMProp short-circuits on `if (value === '')` by reading typeof el[key] and taking the boolean path identically in both environments, so :hidden="''" (the unmountOnHide:true case, 2 of the 4 hidden assertions in this file) reflects '' everywhere and looks safe. REVISED RULE: an IDL-name attribute assertion is suspect when the binding can carry a non-empty STRING, not only when the name appears in the sweep's table. CONSEQUENCE BEYOND THE TEST: hidden="until-found" is the entire premise of CollapsibleContent.vue:88-93, the beforematch listener that opens the collapsible and emits contentFound when browser find-in-page reveals hidden content. Under jsdom that attribute value can never reach the DOM at all, so the feature is structurally untestable there; Chromium is the first environment in this repo where it is even reachable, though neither suite drives find-in-page.

THE TIERING ROW. PORT-INVENTORY tiers this T2-mechanical; that is right about the WORK and wrong about the COMPONENT, and this is the first file where those two came apart. CollapsibleContent.vue:65-67 measures itself with getBoundingClientRect() and publishes the result as --reka-collapsible-content-height / --reka-collapsible-content-width, which is textbook T3 geometry. Measured on the _Collapsible.vue fixture in both environments. [jsdom] closed 0px/0px, open 0px/0px, unmountOnHide:false closed 0px/0px — every state, both axes, always zero, and getBoundingClientRect/offsetHeight agree at 0 throughout. [Chromium] default closed 0px/0px (nothing is mounted); OPEN 24px height / 414px width; unmountOnHide:false CLOSED 0px height / 414px WIDTH. That last cell is the one jsdom cannot represent: hidden="until-found" maps to content-visibility:hidden rather than display:none, so the box keeps its width and loses its height — which is exactly the asymmetry the two custom properties exist to express, since the documented use is a CSS transition from height 0 to var(--reka-collapsible-content-height). AND NOTHING ASSERTS ANY OF IT. Not the original, not the port (an added `it` would be INVENTED). Mutation-verified: replacing both values with a literal `0px` in CollapsibleContent.vue leaves the jsdom suite 11/11 green AND the browser port 9 passed + 2 expected-fail green. THE COVERAGE DELTA MAKES THE SAME POINT FROM THE OTHER SIDE: +9/-0, and none of the 9 is Chromium's doing — Presence/usePresence.ts L162-169 is the onUnmounted teardown block, Presence/Presence.ts L86 is the ref callback's null branch on unmount, shared/useForwardExpose.ts L68 is the known ref-detach line. All three are the #auto-unmount harness freebie (vitest-browser-vue registers beforeEach(cleanup); the jsdom original never unmounts). The browser executes ZERO extra lines of Collapsible's own source, because the measurement line was always executed — it just always returned 0. A covered line is not a tested behaviour, and here it is not even a measured one.

`should call `update:open` prop with `false` value` does wrapper.vm.$emit('update:open', false) and then asserts the wrapper emitted update:open with false. The component is not involved at any point: the test emits the event and checks the event was emitted, which is a test of Vue's $emit. It is unfailable by any change to Collapsible whatsoever — deleting CollapsibleRoot's useVModel, its onOpenToggle, or the trigger's @click leaves it green. Ported under rule 4 (a name describing something that does not happen gets fixed in the test, never renamed) by clicking the trigger of the defaultOpen fixture instead. Measured: screen.emitted('update:open') is [[false]] after exactly one click, because _Collapsible.vue forwards emits through useForwardPropsEmits, so the name is now literally true and the test can now fail. Same shape and same precedent as Slider#form-submit-button (synthetic form submit -> real submit button). TRANSLATION-TABLE GAP WORTH LANDING, because it will recur: vitest-browser-vue's render result exposes container, baseElement, locator, debug, unmount, emitted, rerender and the document-scoped getBy* helpers (dist/pure-epEwB8Ps.js L33-45) — and NO `vm` and no `wrapper`. So `wrapper.vm.<anything>` has no mechanical translation at all; an original that reaches through .vm must be rewritten around a real interaction. That is usually an improvement rather than a cost, since reaching for .vm is generally how a component test stops testing the component.

NOT VACUOUS IN EITHER ENVIRONMENT — censused by node count rather than by bucket, reading `incomplete` as well as `passes` and `inapplicable`, in both projects. Default (closed) fixture: jsdom 8 passing rules with nodes / 0 violations / 0 incomplete; Chromium 8 / 0 / 0. unmountOnHide:false (closed): jsdom 8 / 0 / 0; Chromium 9 / 0 / 0. Both audits genuinely reach the component — button-name:1 and nested-interactive:1 run everywhere, and aria-allowed-attr / aria-conditional-attr / aria-prohibited-attr / aria-valid-attr / aria-valid-attr-value all carry a node. The default censuses differ by exactly two rules and both are explained: jsdom carries aria-hidden-body:1 that Chromium does not (the Separator#axe-context-detached-mount artifact — VTU leaves the component detached, so vitest-axe re-parses outerHTML into document.body and audits with body as the context) and Chromium carries color-contrast:1 in its place. That is the ordinary shape, and it confirms Toggle#axe-census's qualifier from the other side: color-contrast IS the one rule the browser adds, and it applies here precisely because this fixture has text ('Trigger', 'Content') where Toggle's contentless button had none. Chromium's extra ninth rule in the unmountOnHide:false census is avoid-inline-spacing:1, which fires on the content element only there — with unmountOnHide:true the closed content is display:none and axe skips it, while hidden="until-found" is content-visibility:hidden and axe still examines it. Opened (not asserted by any test, probed): Chromium color-contrast rises to 2 nodes and duplicate-id-aria:1 appears, because aria-controls only resolves once rootContext.contentId is populated. Zero violations in every state, on both sides, so the axe assertion never fires — which is not the same as it being strong; see #mutation.

Three mutations, each run in BOTH projects, source restored from a backup and confirmed clean with git diff --stat afterwards. (1) Replace both content size custom properties with a literal 0px: jsdom 11/11 green, browser 9 passed + 2 expected-fail — see #content-size-vars. (2) Delete :aria-controls="rootContext.contentId" from CollapsibleTrigger.vue: jsdom green, browser green. The trigger's association with the content it controls can be removed outright and nothing in either suite notices, axe included — aria-conditional-attr and aria-valid-attr-value both still pass, because an absent attribute is not an invalid one. (3) Delete :aria-expanded="rootContext.open.value": jsdom 11/11 GREEN, browser 3 red. READ (3) CAREFULLY, BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO BOOK AS A WIN AND IS NOT ONE: no `it` in either file asserts aria-expanded, and the port only goes red because three of its hooks use expect.element(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false') to settle Vue's flush after a real click. That settle is genuinely necessary — a Playwright click is a round trip to the browser where the original's un-awaited second trigger('click') got away with a microtask — and choosing the component's own state attribute for it is a free side benefit, but the discrimination is a property of THIS PORT, not of browser mode and not of the original. NET: the whole ARIA contract of CollapsibleTrigger (aria-expanded, aria-controls) is asserted by nobody in either suite, and a green axe run does not substitute for it. Cost note for the AGENTS.md budget entry: mutation (3)'s three failures burned 30018ms + 14949ms + 14963ms of locator timeout, against ~1.0s for the entire green jsdom run — a browser mutation loop on a file whose settle assertions are retrying matchers is ~60x slower to answer per red test.

FOUR OF THE ELEVEN TESTS HAVE A DECORATIVE BODY, and port:parity cannot see it because the assertion count is unchanged. Both `should open the content` tests and `should open the content by default` locate the content with `content = await findByText(wrapper.element, CONTENT_TEXT)` in a hook and then assert `expect(wrapper.text()).toContain(content.innerHTML)`. content.innerHTML IS the string 'Content' and the element was just located inside wrapper — so the assertion reads "the container's text contains text found in the container", which is true by construction. All the discrimination lives in the hook: findByText rejects when the content never appears, so the tests do fail if opening breaks, but nothing in the `it` body contributes. The unmountOnHide:false `should close the content` has the same shape in its third assertion — expect(wrapper.text()).toContain(content.innerHTML) is trivially true whenever unmountOnHide is false, since CollapsibleContent.vue:117 renders the slot unconditionally in that mode. Only the default-mode `should close the content` (a `not.toContain` against a genuinely unmounted slot) can fail on its own assertion. Ported faithfully rather than repaired. One thing the port had to do explicitly that the original got by accident: a vitest locator is lazy, so getByText(...) throws nothing (Switch's second vacuity), and the hook now carries `await expect.element(located).toBeInTheDocument()` where findByText's rejection had been an implicit assertion. Equivalent strength, but written down instead of inherited from the query API. Also checked and NOT a problem here: getByText defaults to a substring match in vitest locators — passed { exact: true } throughout; without it the query still resolves, because nothing else in this fixture contains the string 'Content' (the trigger reads 'Trigger').

THE BATCH CONTROL. Coverage is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two environments - 40 lines in both, 0 lost, 0 gained, same 4 instrumented files, same uncovered lines, same branch gaps - and the port cost 1.9x wall clock (browser 1.30s vs jsdom 0.70s; test execution 98ms vs 28ms). Nothing was deleted because the original installs no stub, mocks nothing, runs no axe and touches no geometry. CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW, and the correction is the useful part: this row previously claimed the two suites were EQUALLY STRONG on the evidence of a 7-mutation matrix. That claim was false as written, because the matrix had a hole exactly where this file is most exposed - see #mutation-matrix and #tag-not-role. The port had translated `wrapper.find("button")` (a TAG query) to `screen.getByRole("button")` (a ROLE query) in `should render button element correctly`, and on a component whose entire job is choosing which element to render those are not equivalent: with Primitive mutated to serve `as: "button"` as `h("div", { role: "button" })`, the jsdom original went red and the port stayed 15/15 green. Reproduced independently before fixing. The port now asserts the tag (`container.querySelector("button")`) with the role locator kept as an added strengthening, and goes red on that mutation in 66ms. WHAT THE ROW SHOULD HAVE SAID, and now does: after the fix, all EIGHT mutations are detected identically by both environments, and on this file browser mode buys nothing and costs 1.9x. But `no difference found` was a conclusion about my matrix, not about the two environments, and a matrix that only mutates the things the port already asserts cannot discover an assertion the port dropped. Checked and clean: the two Switch vacuities do not apply (pure @vue/test-utils original, zero @testing-library queries - one grep); and the attribute hazard is negative on all 6 attribute names asserted here (type, class, id, data-parent-attr, data-child-attr, data-type) - five take Vue s setAttribute path because `key in el` is false (including `type`, since HTMLDivElement has no `type` IDL property), `id` is the one prop-path binding and Chromium reflects it exactly as jsdom does. Since Primitive IS the prop-to-DOM layer, that is about as strong a negative as the hazard can get.

MUTATION, 8 of them, run against BOTH projects - and the eighth is the one that matters, because it was found by the REVIEWER and not by me. (A) Slot.ts:13 comment-skipping removed (findIndex -> 0): `should by pass the comment tag` red in both, so that test is real in both and the compiler is NOT stripping the comment. (B) Slot.ts:27 mergeProps argument order swapped: 4 red in both - merge class together / after update / replace parent attributes / asChild=true. (C) Slot.ts:29 cloneVNode without the `{...vnode, props:{}}` reset (the pre-fix version): 3 red in both. (D) Slot.ts merge applied only on the FIRST render (per-instance counter): EXACTLY ONE red in both, `should merge child s class after update`, so that test is load-bearing and genuinely distinct from `merge together` - not obvious from reading them. (E) Primitive.ts:56 asChild ignored: 1 red in both. (F) Primitive.ts:52 default `as` div -> span: 3 red in both. (G) Slot.ts multi-child attrs sprayed onto every child: `should pass custom attribute to first element` red in both, the positive case for that test s two toBeUndefined assertions. (H) ADDED AFTER REVIEW - Primitive.ts serves `as: "button"` as `h("div", { ...attrs, role: "button" })` instead of a real <button>, i.e. Primitive stops honouring `as` for buttons and silently loses form submission, implicit keyboard activation and disabled semantics. BEFORE the fix: jsdom 1 red (`should render button element correctly`), browser port 15/15 GREEN. AFTER the fix: both red, browser in 66ms. WHAT A-G MISSED, stated plainly because this is the transferable part: every one of A-G mutates a VALUE the port already reads - an attribute, a class string, a tag name, a merge order. None of them substitutes one ELEMENT for a role-equivalent one, which is the only mutation class that can expose a tag-query-translated-to-role-query. So the matrix could not have found the port s one real weakening, and its `no environment-specific difference` result was sound about the seven things it tested and silent about the eighth. A mutation matrix built by the person who wrote the port inherits that port s blind spots; that is the argument for the split-context reviewer, and here it paid. Cost note, confirmed three more times: a failing retrying matcher burns the full locator timeout - the same red assertion costs ~14990ms in the browser against 1-12ms under jsdom, and that applies to NEGATIVE matchers too (`.not.toHaveAttribute` going red took 14985ms). Corollary used in the fix: put the cheap non-retrying assertion FIRST, which is why H now fails in 66ms rather than ~15s.

AN ASSERTION THAT CANNOT FAIL, IN EITHER ENVIRONMENT, and the only test in the file that mutation could not kill. `should not throw error when multiple child elements exists` ends with `expect(() => wrapper()).not.toThrowError(/invalid children/)`. Three independent reasons it asserts nothing, the first two measured: (1) the string `invalid children` appears exactly once in the repo - Presence.ts:66 - and Primitive.ts / Slot.ts / renderSlotFragments.ts import nothing from Presence and contain no `throw` at all; grepped every package in node_modules/.pnpm too, no dependency ever produces that message, so the regex matches something this code path cannot emit. (2) `not.toThrow(regex)` PASSES when the function throws a NON-matching error - verified with a throwaway probe (`expect(() => { throw new Error("boom, totally unrelated") }).not.toThrowError(/invalid children/)` passes). So the assertion is green for `throws nothing` AND for `throws anything else`. (3) It is redundant regardless: the preceding `expect(wrapper().findAll("div").length).toBe(3)` calls the same factory first, so ANY throw already fails the test one line earlier - verified by mutating Slot to throw `boom: unrelated message` on multi-child input, which turns the test red at assertion 1. The test name describes assertion 2; all the work is done by assertion 1, which is a near-duplicate of `should renders multiple child elements`. Ported verbatim per rule 4 (the name is mislabelled, not describing something that does not happen) with a comment pointing here. Not fixable inside the rules: deleting the assertion would be WEAKENED, rewriting it would be a rename.

TWO REACHABLE BRANCHES NO TEST REACHES, measured twice per the batch-4 rule because the first framing was wrong. Slot.ts branch map is identical in both environments: L9 `if (!slots.default) return null` [0,13] and L14 `if (firstNonCommentChildrenIndex === -1) return children` [0,13] - never taken. Measured twice: re-ran istanbul over 4 CONSUMER suites that drive Primitive hard (NumberField, PinInput, Avatar, TagsInput - 115 tests, 371 Slot renders) and both branches are STILL [0,371]. Verified they are reachable rather than dead, with a throwaway jsdom probe (deleted): `<Primitive as="template" />` with no slot renders `""`, and `<Primitive as="template" data-parent-attr><!-- only a comment --></Primitive>` renders `<!-- only a comment -->` and SILENTLY DROPS the parent attribute, because the -1 branch returns the raw children without merging attrs. Note the shape of the second one: the file has a test NAMED `should by pass the comment tag`, and it covers only the comment-then-element half of the comment logic; the all-comments half is untested everywhere. The same measurement corrected a claim I nearly filed: Primitive.ts:58 `SELF_CLOSING_TAGS.includes(asTag)` is [0,16] in Primitive.test.ts and looks equally dead, but the consumer run shows 311 hits - `as="input"` and `as="img"` are used by ~10 components. So that one is a gap in THIS file only, not in the suite. Nothing added: an extra `it` would be INVENTED.

A QUALIFIER FOR THE `reading an attribute after an interaction needs a retry first` GOTCHA, measured because the port has the one test that interacts. Claim: an awaited `locator.click()` has ALREADY crossed Vue s flush by the time it returns, for a synchronous state update. Measured on the `should merge child s class after update` fixture (a click flips `isActive`, which re-renders `:data-active`): a plain SYNCHRONOUS `section.getAttribute("data-active")` immediately after `await page.elementLocator(el).click()` reads the NEW value, 4 runs out of 4. Mechanism, so this is not read as luck: the click round-trips to the Playwright server over CDP, i.e. many macrotasks, while Vue flushes on a microtask scheduled inside the event handler that already ran in the page. Scope carefully - this holds for synchronous reactive updates only, and says nothing about a watcher that awaits, a transition, or anything on a timer. Practical consequence: the retrying `expect.element` settle is the right DEFAULT (free on the happy path, and the only safe choice when you do not know what the handler does) but it is not what makes such a port correct, so it must not be used as the excuse for dropping the original s exact synchronous read - that is exactly the Progress#retry-widens-timing weakening. The port keeps BOTH: a retrying `expect.element(section).toHaveAttribute(...)` and then the original s synchronous class read. Verified the synchronous read is the assertion doing the work - under mutation (D) the test fails at that exact line.

A TRANSLATION-TABLE GAP, and it silently changes what a ported query means. `wrapper.find(sel)` / `wrapper.findAll(sel)` on a VUEWRAPPER go through `findAllDOMElements` (vue-test-utils.esm-bundler.mjs:7046-7056), which matches the component s ROOT nodes as well as their descendants; `findAll` on a DOMWRAPPER is plain `element.querySelectorAll` (L7247) and does NOT include the wrapped element. The two are different and this file uses both, one line apart: `should renders multiple child elements` does `wrapper.find("div").findAll("div")` where the outer find returns the ROOT div (only possible because VueWrapper.find is root-inclusive) and the inner findAll is descendants-only = 3; `should not throw error when multiple child elements exists` does `wrapper.findAll("div")` on a fragment root where all 3 divs ARE roots = also 3. Translating both to the same container-scoped querySelectorAll would give 3 and 3 and look right, while meaning something different in each case. The browser equivalents: VueWrapper.find/findAll -> `screen.container.querySelector(All)`, which is root-inclusive because `vitest-browser-vue` unwraps VTU s own mount div (pure-epEwB8Ps.js:29 `unwrapNode(wrapper.parentElement)`) so every root is a DIRECT CHILD of the container; DOMWrapper.findAll -> `element.querySelectorAll` on that element. Also confirmed here: no locator can address a bare `<div>` or a href-less `<a>` (both role generic), so 9 of the 15 tests stay on `container.querySelector` - on a rendering primitive the locator API is mostly unusable, which is the opposite of the T2 norm.

THE ISTANBUL BRANCH MAP FOR THE THREE COLLAPSIBLE SFCs IS IDENTICAL IN THE TWO ENVIRONMENTS — same untaken branches, same uncovered statements, only the hit counts differ. That is the sharpest available statement of what this port did and did not buy: browser mode executes not one branch of Collapsible that jsdom did not. What both suites leave dead: (a) CollapsibleContent.vue L89-91, the body of the beforematch listener (rootContext.onOpenToggle() plus emits('contentFound')) — zero hits in both, and per #hidden-until-found it is not even reachable under jsdom, since hidden="until-found" can never land in that DOM; (b) CollapsibleRoot.vue L67-68, the `if (disabled.value) return` guard in onOpenToggle, branch [0,8] — NO TEST IN EITHER SUITE EVER PASSES disabled, so the whole disabled prop of Collapsible is untested, including the three :data-disabled bindings that go with it (CollapsibleRoot L83 [0,19], CollapsibleContent L111 [0,55], CollapsibleTrigger L28 [0,19], all zero on the disabled side); (c) CollapsibleTrigger.vue L22, :type="as === 'button' ? 'button' : undefined" is [19,0] — only the default `as` is ever rendered, so the one thing stopping a Collapsible trigger from submitting its enclosing form is untested, exactly as in Toggle#form-value-never-submits; (d) CollapsibleContent.vue L54-55, the `if (!node) return` early return. Reported, not fixed — an added `it` would be INVENTED (rule 4) and a patch is forbidden (rule 7). Method note for the queue: this took one extra istanbul run per project and answered a question the +9/-0 line count could not, which is the whole point of AGENTS.md's "a covered line is not a tested behaviour" — here every line of the disabled path is COVERED (the ternaries evaluate on every render) while every branch of it is dead.

A TRANSLATION-TABLE HAZARD THAT ALREADY HAD A WARNING, AND THE WARNING WAS NOT ENOUGH. AGENTS.md carries `wrapper.findAll("button") -> screen.getByRole("button").elements() - re-probe the equivalence per file, tag<->role only coincides sometimes`. I read it and fell in anyway, on the one file in the library where the substitution is most dangerous. The defect: `should render button element correctly` translated `wrapper.find("button").exists()` to `expect.element(screen.getByRole("button")).toBeInTheDocument()`. Measured (mutation H, reproduced independently before fixing): with Primitive serving `as: "button"` as `h("div", { ...attrs, role: "button" })`, jsdom goes red and the role-only port stays 15/15 green - so Primitive could stop honouring `as: "button"` entirely, losing form submission, implicit keyboard activation and disabled semantics, and the test NAMED `should render button element correctly` would still pass. Fixed with `expect(screen.container.querySelector("button")).not.toBeNull()` as the translation, role locator kept alongside as a strengthening; now red in 66ms. WHY `re-probe per file` IS THE WRONG SHAPE OF RULE: it asks for a per-file measurement whose expected answer is `they agree`, and they DID agree here - the unmutated fixture renders a real <button> that has role button, so any probe of the AS-IS component confirms the substitution and licenses it. The equivalence that matters is not `do tag and role select the same node today` but `can the component change the tag without changing the role`, which a probe of the current DOM cannot answer. PROPOSED ROW, sharper and checkable without measuring anything: `wrapper.find("button") / findAll("button") -> container.querySelector(All)("button") when the TAG is the subject; getByRole only when the ROLE is the subject. Never translate a tag query to a role query on a component that chooses its own tag (Primitive and anything with as / asChild - i.e. every component in this library). Role and tag agree on an unmutated fixture, so probing cannot license the swap.` NOTE THE BLAST RADIUS, because it is larger than one file: `as` / `asChild` is Primitive s public API and every component here renders through it, so ANY ported test asserting a tag on a reka component is a candidate. The narrow consolation measured here: the same substitution at the `asChild=true` test has NO exposure, because that <button> comes from the test s own slot string and no source change can alter its tag. So the rule bites only where the tag under assertion is the one the component CHOSE.

A REGRESSION THE REVIEWER CAUGHT IN THIS PORT, AND THE RECIPE IN AGENTS.MD THAT CAUSED IT. The old rule prescribed "assert twice - retrying expect.element first, then the original exact read". Applied here it produced two dead assertions. MUTATION: delay the no-animation dispatch('UNMOUNT') by 500ms. jsdom failed 3 tests while the first port stayed fully green, because a retrying matcher settles THE ASSERTION, not a generic flush; putting it before the same synchronous read makes that read unfailable. REPAIR: wait only on a distinct pre-interaction state where needed, await the real click, and keep the original bare synchronous read with no extra nextTick. The no-tick version was re-run against the same 500ms mutation and both exact browser close assertions still failed immediately. `wrapper.attributes('x')` therefore translates to `el.getAttribute('x')` + toBe here when exact timing matters, not to a retrying toHaveAttribute. The recipe also failed on its motivating Progress example: moving the fixture flip from 200ms to 900ms made the jsdom original fail while the retrying port stayed green. ORACLE BLIND SPOT: the broken Presence version reported more assertions than the original while being weaker; assertion count is not assertion strength in either direction. See browser-mode#nexttick-audit.

A QUARANTINE SILENTLY DISARMS EVERY OTHER ASSERTION IN ITS TEST, AND port:parity CANNOT SEE IT — it counts assertions, and the count is unchanged. Found by the reviewer, not by me; I had filed it as a caveat rather than a row, and it is worse than a caveat. MECHANISM, confirmed from source and by measurement: it.fails is a boolean on the whole test. @vitest/runner packages/runner/src/run.ts:765 does `if (test.fails) { if (state === 'pass') -> fail else -> pass }`, at the very end of runTest, so ANY non-pass state flips to pass. The nested `should close the content` has three assertions; assertion 2 (getAttribute('hidden') === '') throws unconditionally in Chromium, so the test is green no matter what assertions 1 and 3 do — and assertion 2 is not verified either, it merely has to be one of the throwers. Assertion 3 never even executes, which also dents PORTING.md 2.1's justification for preferring .fails over .skip ("the body still runs and still contributes coverage"): the body only runs UP TO the throw. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY LOST, mutation-verified in both projects, source restored and confirmed clean afterwards: (1) data-state 'closed' -> 'BROKEN' in CollapsibleContent.vue: jsdom 1 failed, port GREEN. (2) the slot v-if="rootContext.unmountOnHide.value ? present : true" -> v-if="present", which breaks unmountOnHide:false outright: jsdom 1 failed, port GREEN. So the entire contract of unmountOnHide:false in the closed state — content stays mounted, data-state flips to closed — had no detector left in the browser suite while jsdom caught both. FIXED, and the fix is the interesting part. Probed every escape route. Reordering does NOT work: green means "something threw", so putting the failing assertion last still swallows breakage in the others (verified — assertions after a thrower do not run at all). try/catch and re-throw does not work, for the same reason. expect.soft does not work: soft failures still fail the test. AND EVERY HOOK POSITION IS ABSORBED TOO — measured with a throwaway 5-case probe: it.fails absorbs a beforeEach assertion error, a beforeEach TIMEOUT (which is how the reviewer first noticed this, a hook timing out at 30013ms while the test reported a tick), an afterEach error, and an onTestFinished error. All five green. THE ROUTE THAT WORKS: a hook is absorbed only for the .fails test itself. The `given a Collapsible with unmountOnHide:false` beforeEach also runs for the TWO tests in that block that are NOT quarantined (`should pass axe accessibility tests` and `when clicking the trigger > should open the content`), and for those a hook failure is a real failure. Moving the two orphaned assertions there restores both detectors — re-verified against both mutations above: the port now goes red on 2 tests each, i.e. MORE detection than the jsdom original's 1. No rename, no invented test, no weakened assertion, no source patch, and the per-test assertion counts are untouched because countAssertions only walks `it` bodies. The assertions also read honestly there: the describe says "given a Collapsible with unmountOnHide:false" and they assert exactly that given. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, worth recording because it works and is still worse: adding the same two assertions to the non-quarantined `should pass axe accessibility tests` body also catches both mutations (measured). It was rejected because the failure then surfaces under a name about accessibility, which misdirects triage, and because it would establish "stash orphaned assertions in a neighbouring test" as the pattern for the ~60 remaining files. The hook placement gets the same detection with the failure attributed to setup. GENERALISES TO EVERY REMAINING QUARANTINE: the hazard is exactly "a quarantined test with more than one assertion". Slider#axe and AlertDialog's quarantines are single-assertion and therefore safe; this is the first multi-assertion one, and there will be more. RULE: when quarantining, count the assertions first — if there is more than one, the non-throwing ones must be relocated to a hook shared with a non-quarantined test, or they are gone.

THE COLLAPSIBLE HALF OF Accordion/Accordion.visual.browser.test.ts#aria-controls-empty-at-rest, measured in Chromium on the _Collapsible.vue fixture: at rest the trigger renders aria-controls="" while the content already has id reka-collapsible-content-v-N; defaultOpen=true is empty at rest too (open and linked are independent — only `open` is a ref); one click fills it. Cause is CollapsibleRoot.vue:61 `contentId: ''` (plain string in a non-reactive context) read by CollapsibleTrigger.vue:25 at first render, written by CollapsibleContent.vue:35 `||= useId()` during the content's later setup, never invalidated. Quarantined as it.fails in Collapsible.aria-controls.browser.test.ts — a separate unpaired file, because port:parity rejects INVENTED tests inside a port file. ALSO MEASURED: this bug CANNOT be expressed as an ARIA snapshot — toMatchAriaInlineSnapshot of the root is byte-identical (`- button "Trigger" [expanded]` / `- text: Content`) with aria-controls empty and filled, because ivya's tree node carries only checked/disabled/expanded/level/pressed/selected/active + /url + /placeholder (read out of @vitest/browser dist/expect-element.js) and no relation attribute. A sibling green test pins that blindness so a future Vitest that renders relations turns it red. Upstream v2 @ b32f255 (2026-08-13) has the identical three lines. UPSTREAM HISTORY (gh, 2026-08-20): known to the maintainer and dropped. Issue unovue/reka-ui#2521 (2026-03-16, 'VoiceOver does not announce expanded/collapsed') led zernonia to open PR #2522 the same day — 'fix(Collapsible): make contentId reactive to fix VoiceOver aria-controls' — whose body states the exact diagnosis ('On initial render aria-controls="" (empty)') and whose diff is the Ref<string> fix across the same three files. The reporter then found their VoiceOver settings were the cause of the *announcement* symptom, the issue closed as user error (2026-03-18), and the PR was closed unmerged the next day. No open issue names the empty aria-controls itself; the related open work (#2597/#2774/#2882/#2883) is the opposite shape — triggers that keep an aria-controls pointing at UNMOUNTED popup content. NOT A BROWSER-MODE WIN, measured: the same _Collapsible.vue fixture mounted under jsdom (VTU mount, defaultOpen) reads aria-controls="" at rest, content id reka-collapsible-content-v-0, and the filled id after trigger('click') — identical to Chromium, because Vue's render order is the environment's, not the DOM's. jsdom had this attribute empty in every Accordion/Collapsible test since they were written; grep: zero aria-controls assertions in either runner's Accordion or Collapsible tests before this. What surfaced it was the visual-sheet WORKFLOW — render the story as a page loads, inspect BEFORE any interaction (the click is the one action that repairs the attribute), and write exact assertions for the relations a screenshot cannot show — plus axe being structurally blind to valid-but-empty ARIA in both runners. Book it as a workflow finding, the way cleanup() teardown coverage is booked as the harness's, not Chromium's.

8/8 tests, 43/43 assertions; checklist, parity --complete and coverage all clean. T2, no stubs to delete and no geometry workaround needed (the segments are block-level, 414x24 in Chromium, so unlike Switch/Toggle no beforeAll <style> is required). The +5 gained lines are shared/date/useDateField.ts L413,L414,L422,L435,L436 — the two-digit accumulation branch of updateDayOrMonth — and they are NOT a browser-mode win: per PORTING.md 2.2 the question is who earned it, and a throwaway jsdom probe typing '1' then '9' reaches day="1" then day="19" with the same focus move, so the branch is reachable from jsdom and the original simply never typed a second digit. THE ONE THING THAT BREAKS IN BROWSER MODE FOR THE WHOLE DATE FAMILY. The original does user.keyboard('{19}') — a single keydown whose event.key is the two-character string "19". No keyboard can emit that; only a synthetic dispatcher can. vitest's playwright provider says so structurally: keyboardImplementation (@vitest/browser-playwright/src/commands/keyboard.ts:86-91) tests the parsed key against a VALID_KEYS set of real Playwright key names and falls back to page.keyboard.insertText(key) for anything else — and insertText fires NO keydown at all. Measured with a literal port: the day segment stays "dd" / aria-valuetext="Empty" and focus never leaves it; 7 of 8 tests passed, that one failed. Ported as two real digits ('19'), which reaches the identical state (updateDayOrMonth: 1 -> value 1 no advance; 9 -> total 19 <= 28 advance) through a gesture a user can perform. Not quarantined: it.fails would have absorbed the other four assertions in that test (the Collapsible rule). Blast radius, grepped: 8 call sites in 4 files — DateField.test.ts L432 {19}, L435 {1111}, L457 {19}, L459 {1980}; TimeField.test.ts L69 {11}; DatePicker.test.ts L364 {2020}, L368 {45}; DateRangeField.test.ts L67 {19}. Every one silently becomes a no-op keystroke in browser mode. The year sites ({1111},{1980},{2020}) need per-site verification rather than a blind 1:1 rewrite, because 4 real digits go through year accumulation rather than one key. Note the failure mode: insertText into the contenteditable does NOT leak text either, because handleSegmentBeforeInput preventDefaults it — so the symptom is purely "focus did not advance", which reads like a focus bug and is not one.

Non-obvious and load-bearing for all 12 remaining date-family files: vitest.global.ts sets process.env.TZ = 'US/Eastern' in the NODE process, and that reaches Chromium. Measured inside the tester iframe: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone === 'America/New_York' (the canonical alias of US/Eastern) on a machine whose /etc/localtime is Europe/Berlin, i.e. it is the globalSetup value and not the host's. navigator.language is en-US in both environments. So @internationalized/date fixtures — CalendarDate, CalendarDateTime and toZoned(..., 'America/New_York') — render byte-identically in both projects and the ZonedDateTime test needed no adjustment. It works by inheritance (Playwright launches the browser with the parent process env), NOT by configuration: nothing sets browser.timezoneId. If a future change launches the browser with an explicit env, or reorders globalSetup relative to browser launch, every date-family port shifts timezone at once and the failures will look like component bugs. Worth pinning explicitly before T3.

Mutation result: deleting tabindex from every segment (commonSegmentAttrs 'tabindex: props.disabled ? undefined : 0' -> 'undefined') leaves ALL 8 tests green in BOTH projects. Verified the mutation was live rather than optimised away — probed the rendered DOM with it applied: every segment reports tabindex=null. The reason is that the segments are contenteditable="true", which makes them focusable and sequentially focusable in Chromium natively, and which @testing-library/user-event's own focusable selector also matches — so the Tab loop in 'navigates between the fields' proves nothing about the component's tabindex in either environment. The prop is not dead in production (it is what removes segments from the tab order when disabled, and what the literal segments deliberately lack) — it is dead to the tests, and no test in this file uses disabled. Forbidden to fix by rule 7.

The negative results, stated plainly, because 'not vacuous' is the normal answer and is worth recording. Three mutations, each run against both projects. (1) focusNext() made direction-aware (currentSegmentIndex + 1 -> + (dir === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1), i.e. reintroducing the exact bug its source comment guards against): 'advances focus ... in RTL' goes RED in both. (2) handleSegmentKeydown's Tab escape removed ('if (e.key !== kbd.TAB)' -> 'if (true)', so Tab is preventDefaulted): both 'navigates between the fields' tests go RED in both projects — user-event honours preventDefault on a Tab keydown just as Chromium does, so the jsdom original was not faking that one. (3) monthSegmentAttrs' aria-label removed: the axe test goes RED in both with aria-input-field-name. So the file's assertions are real; the only thing neither suite can fail is #tabindex-untested.

Full axe census by NODE COUNT in both environments, per the AGENTS.md rule that buckets alone lie. NOT vacuous in either: jsdom runs 14 rules with real nodes (aria-allowed-attr 6, aria-allowed-role 7, aria-conditional-attr 6, aria-deprecated-role 7, aria-hidden-focus 5, aria-input-field-name 6, aria-prohibited-attr 6, aria-required-attr 7, aria-roles 7, aria-valid-attr-value 6, aria-valid-attr 6, avoid-inline-spacing 6, duplicate-id-aria 1, tabindex 6), 0 violations, 71 inapplicable. Chromium runs those same 14 with identical node counts plus exactly one more — color-contrast, 8 nodes, passing. Under jsdom color-contrast sits in `incomplete` with ZERO nodes, i.e. it did not run; a bucket-only census would have called that 'the rule ran'. Two things worth carrying to the rest of the family: the textbook one-extra-rule result holds here because the fixture has text, and unlike Separator there is NO aria-hidden-body artifact in the jsdom column (it is inapplicable in both), so the detached-mount context widening does not always add a rule.

Deliberate sweep for the two silent vacuities, since this family is @testing-library/vue + @testing-library/user-event and both traps leave assertion counts unchanged. (1) getByText substring: NOT APPLICABLE, and not just here — grepped getByText/queryByText/findByText across DateField, TimeField, Calendar, RangeCalendar, DatePicker, DateRangePicker and DateRangeField: ZERO hits. The family queries entirely by data-testid, so the whole family is immune to that trap. (2) lazy locator: APPLICABLE, and it is concentrated in the shared setup() helper rather than in test bodies — there are no bare getBy* statements in any test, but setup() resolves eight getByTestId calls (start/end x month/day/year, plus 'input' and 'label', the last two never used afterwards) whose only purpose is the throw @testing-library performs on a miss. A literal port to lazy locators would have deleted eight existence assertions without changing the expect count. Preserved by resolving each with .element(), which both reproduces the throw and hands the tests the same raw HTMLElement the original held — which in turn is what lets every assertion in the file stay the original's exact synchronous expect(el).toHaveFocus() / toHaveTextContent() rather than a retrying expect.element. Recommended as the standard setup() translation for the remaining 12 date-family files.

7/7 tests, 16/16 assertions; checklist --complete, parity --complete, coverage and the jsdom original all exit 0, first try. T2, no stubs to delete (the original installs none). SSR WORKS IN THE BROWSER PROJECT, UNMODIFIED. THIS UNBLOCKS Accordion AND EVERY OTHER ssr-FLAGGED FILE. Measured, not assumed: `import { renderToString } from "@vue/server-renderer"` resolves and runs inside the tester iframe, createSSRApp(...).config.idPrefix + renderToString(app) returns the full 1127-char string, container.innerHTML = html followed by clientApp.mount(container) hydrates, and vi.spyOn(console,"warn"|"error") observes Vue hydration warnings. MECHANISM, so nobody has to re-derive it: @vue/server-renderer@3.5.17 package exports have NO `browser` condition — only types/node/module/import/require — so Vite takes `import` and serves dist/server-renderer.esm-bundler.js. That build is a pure string builder over @vue/shared with no node: import in it, which is why the usual "the vue browser condition gives you runtime-only" fear does not apply. SFCs compiled by @vitejs/plugin-vue for the client (render, not ssrRender) render fine because Vue falls back to walking the client vnode tree. THE NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS ARE FALSIFIABLE, verified by constructing the positive case rather than assuming: a throwaway probe hydrating a nuxt-N server tree with an other-N client tree produced, in Chromium, `[Vue warn]: Hydration attribute mismatch on ... rendered on server: id="reka-tabs-nuxt-1-trigger-account" ... expected on client: id="reka-tabs-other-1-trigger-account"` plus `Hydration completed but contains mismatches.`, both captured by the spies. Also confirmed the asserted substring is a real Vue message and not a typo: runtime-core.esm-bundler.js:2192 builds `Hydration ${MismatchTypeString[type]} mismatch on` with MismatchTypeString[4]="attribute" (:2258-2264) — there is no literal "Hydration attribute mismatch" in the bundle to grep for, which is exactly the shape of thing that looks vacuous and is not. Mutation-verified end to end: swapping the branch order in shared/useId.ts so vue.useId wins over ConfigProvider (the bug the test guards) turns the test RED in both projects, identically, on the same assertion. RECOMMENDATION FOR Accordion: port the SSR block literally, change nothing, and spend the effort on #ssr-container-leaks instead.

THE ACTUAL COST OF AN SSR TEST IN BROWSER MODE, AND IT IS NOT THE SSR. An SSR/hydration test builds its own container with document.createElement and appends it to document.body; vitest-browser-vue cleanup() only removes containers IT created, so that container — with a live hydrated Vue app inside it — survives every subsequent beforeEach for the rest of the file. Measured in a probe replicating this file test order: at the start of the next test document.body.children.length is 1 and document.querySelectorAll("[role=tab]").length is 2 BEFORE anything is rendered; after render(Tabs) the document holds 4 tabs, and because render getBy* helpers bind to baseElement = document.body (the corrected rule from Teleport), BOTH screen.getByRole("tab").elements() AND page.getByRole("tab").elements() return 4 while screen.container.querySelectorAll returns 2. So a role-query translation of wrapper.findAll("button")[1] would have indexed into the SSR leftovers, and getByRole("tabpanel") returns a mixed 2 (one leftover, one fixture) because the hidden panels are filtered out. This file is safe because every query in the original is VueWrapper-scoped and therefore translates to container-scoped, but that is luck, not design. RULE FOR THE REMAINING ssr FILES: in any file containing an SSR test, container-scope every query in every OTHER test, or the leftover silently joins the result set. Note the jsdom original has the identical leak and is safe for the identical reason — this is not a browser-mode regression, it is a trap that browser mode document-scoped locator helpers make much easier to fall into. Also note document.body.innerHTML = "" inside the SSR test is safe to keep (the tester iframe body holds nothing but render containers) and is NOT what cleans the leftover up — nothing does.

CLICKING A TAB DOES NOT CHANGE TABS UNDER JSDOM — THE COMPONENT PRIMARY GESTURE IS UNTESTABLE THERE, AND NEITHER SUITE TESTS IT. TabsTrigger.vue activates on `@mousedown.left` (L54), not on click. Measured with matched throwaway probes: VTU second.trigger("click") under jsdom leaves the second trigger data-state="inactive", leaves "Change your password" out of the HTML, and leaves TabsTrigger.vue:54 at istanbul hit count 0; a real locator.click() in Chromium gives data-state="active", renders the content, and takes L54 with hit count 1 and its ctrl-key branches [1] and [1,1]. This is the AGENTS.md #click-fires-no-mousedown rule at its sharpest so far: not one missed coverage line but the whole user-facing activation path. THE GAP: L54 (mousedown activation, including the `event.ctrlKey === false` else-branch that calls preventDefault) and L65 (`@keydown.enter.space` activation) are UNCOVERED IN BOTH PROJECTS — verified from the two coverage-final.json files for the real test pair, statement hits 54=>0 and 65=>0 on both sides, branch@54 [0] and [0,0] under jsdom. So Tabs mouse activation and its Enter/Space activation have no test at all in either suite, and the only reason the file looks well covered is that ArrowRight plus automatic-activation-on-focus reaches the selected state by another road. Forbidden to fix by rule 7 and unfixable by a port anyway — an added `it` would be INVENTED. WORTH ACTING ON ELSEWHERE: browser mode covers both for free the moment anyone adds a click test, and any component in this library that activates on mousedown/pointerdown has the same silent hole in its jsdom suite.

NOT vacuous on either side: 0 violations both, and jsdom already runs 16 rules with real nodes (aria-allowed-attr 4, aria-allowed-role 5, aria-conditional-attr 4, aria-deprecated-role 4, aria-prohibited-attr 4, aria-required-attr 4, aria-required-children 1, aria-required-parent 2, aria-roles 4, aria-valid-attr-value 4, aria-valid-attr 4, avoid-inline-spacing 2, button-name 2, duplicate-id-aria 2, nested-interactive 2, tabindex 4), 69 inapplicable. ALL SIXTEEN GAINED LINES ARE TEARDOWN, SO CHROMIUM EARNED EXACTLY ZERO OF THEM. THE FILE'S MAIN RESULT, and it is about the gesture rather than the component. RadioGroupItem latches isArrowKeyPressed=true on keydown (L66), clears it on keyup (L69), and handleFocus defers its .click() by setTimeout(...,0) (L73-81). `fireEvent.keyDown` dispatches a keydown and NOTHING ELSE, so under jsdom the flag is stuck true for the rest of the file and the deferred click always fires. Machine evidence, not inference: RadioGroupItem.vue:69 is a GAINED line - hit count 0 across the entire jsdom file. In Chromium a complete userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowDown}') sends down+up back to back and Chromium services the input task BEFORE the 0ms timer, so the flag is already false when the timeout runs and the radio is never checked. Traced 10/10 times as keydown -> focusin -> keyup -> setTimeout(0). Measured over 15 isolated renders each: plain '{ArrowDown}' selects 1/15 (the 1 is the first, cold run); '{ArrowDown>}' + sleep(0) + '{/ArrowDown}' selects 15/15. The held form is what the port uses, because it is both the faithful translation of fireEvent.keyDown + await sleep(0) AND the realistic one - a human holds a key for ~80ms, so real users always win this race. What is genuinely proven: (a) the jsdom suite never once executed the keyup reset, so a keyup-handling regression is invisible to it; (b) the component's arrow-key selection depends on winning a race with a 1-macrotask budget, and any zero-delay synthetic press loses it. vitest's userEvent.keyboard(text) takes no delay option (docs/api/browser/interactivity.md:279), so the hold syntax is the only lever.

Chromium-earned, and the mechanism is worth knowing before the T3 overlays. Force-clicking a DISABLED radio delivers ONLY `pointerdown` - no mousedown, no mouseup, no click (measured; confirms that Playwright's force:true skips the actionability WAIT, not the gesture, and Chromium suppresses the rest itself) - and then moves focus to the nearest mouse-focusable ancestor, which is RovingFocusGroup's Primitive. Note that in a fully disabled group focusableItemsCount===0, so that div carries tabindex="-1"; Chromium click-focuses it anyway, because tabindex=-1 is mouse-focusable even though it is not tab-focusable. Consequence inside the component: the group's @mousedown never runs, so isClickFocus stays false, so handleFocus takes the `isKeyboardFocus` branch and runs the full ENTRY-FOCUS algorithm for what was actually a mouse interaction - i.e. the Safari workaround is bypassed precisely in the disabled case. That is what covers RovingFocusGroup.vue L90-L115 and L161 (@blur). None of it is reachable from jsdom, where VTU's DOMWrapper.trigger short-circuits on isDisabled() and never focuses anything.

`wrapper.find('[type="Radio"]')` ports VERBATIM, capital R and all: `type` is on HTML's case-insensitive-attribute-value list, so `[type="Radio"]` matches `<input type="radio">` in Chromium exactly as in jsdom (measured, both true). It stays a container.querySelector rather than becoming a locator for a reason worth noting - `getByRole('radio', { includeHidden: true })` matches TWO elements here, the explicit role="radio" button and the hidden input's implicit role, so getBy* throws. This is the Switch case with the opposite outcome: there the root was role="switch" so the includeHidden role query disambiguated by itself; here the control and its hidden input share a role and only a tag/attribute query separates them.

A real trigger click delivers its own pointerup at the unchanged position — the exact 'accidental pointerup' the guard exists for — which consumes and disarms the guard, so a following real option click selects first try. Verified: the port performs single clicks everywhere and all selection tests pass, and the guard's preventDefault line stays covered because the opening click's own pointerup exercises it.

An open Select is modal: DismissableLayer.vue:173 sets document.body pointer-events:none and Chromium's hit-testing honours it, so every element outside the content — the trigger, the fixture's Close button — is unreachable by ANY pointer, forced clicks included (a forced click dispatches trusted input at coordinates and the browser routes it to <html>). jsdom has no hit-testing, so the original 'clicked' the Close button through the modal, asserting a gesture no user can make. The keyboard detour also fails, for a second measured reason: focusing Close and pressing Enter worked only until SelectContentImpl.vue:129's watch(isPositioned) ran focusSelectedItem and stole focus back to the first item, after which Enter closed BY SELECTION while every assertion still passed — only the coverage oracle caught that the Close handler (SelectUnmountCleanup.vue:19) never ran. The port closes via Escape (the gesture a modal select actually offers) and books L19 as an argued loss.

The multiple-mode 'after opening the modal again' hook fires pointerdown on the trigger while the modal is still open. That gesture is doubly fictional: (1) in a real browser the trigger is inert (see #modal-blocks-outside-clicks) and a press at its coordinates lands on <html>, which is an OUTSIDE press and would dismiss the modal via DismissableLayer's pointerDownOutside -> dismiss; (2) in jsdom it was a state no-op — onOpenChange(true) with open already true — whose only real effect was re-arming the pointerup guard, which is why the very next selection needed two pointerups again. jsdom never saw the dismissal because the outside-press listener registration (utils.ts:126, setTimeout 0) never fires within one test's hook chain. The port's hook is deliberately a no-op wait: the state the describe wants already holds, and the guard-disarm difference is absorbed by single-click selection.

FIRST vi.useFakeTimers() IN BROWSER MODE, and it works: sinon installs on the iframe window, vi.getTimerCount() sees the component's deferred renderPresence update (SelectContent.vue:64), vi.spyOn(window,'clearTimeout') wraps the fake and catches the unmount cleanup, and Playwright interactions plus retrying matchers keep running on real time outside the page. The sharp edge: the DEFAULT toFake set includes requestAnimationFrame and performance, so floating-ui positioning freezes — measured: with the clock frozen, watch(isPositioned)'s focusSelectedItem fired only when a later userEvent RPC let frames through, stealing focus mid-gesture; and a poll loop built on performance.now() deadlocks because the faked clock never advances. Rule: under browser fake timers, never wait on anything positioning- or rAF-dependent, and drive state through paths that need only microtasks (Escape, direct events).

Same family as the getByText substring vacuity in AGENTS.md, but louder — with multiple matches it fails as a strict-mode error instead of silently passing, and with a single match ('Banana' matching only Banana) it would silently widen. FIRST SNAPSHOT PORT. `.browser.test.ts` writes its own `.snap` file, so the jsdom baselines survive for diffing, and the diff is the point: the browser snapshots carry MEASURED scrollbar geometry — `--reka-scroll-area-thumb-height: 18px` (real 200px viewport over ~2200px of wrapped lorem text) and a post-scroll thumb transform of `translate3d(0px, 0.79476px, 0px)` — where jsdom's prototype stubs (offset 500 / scroll 2000 everywhere) made every ratio the same fiction. FOUND BY THE HISTOIRE VISUAL SHEET, measured twice in Chromium. At rest every AccordionTrigger renders aria-controls="" — CollapsibleRoot's contentId is a plain string in a non-reactive context (CollapsibleRoot.vue:62 `contentId: ''`), CollapsibleContent fills it with `||= useId(...)` when IT mounts (CollapsibleContent.vue:35), and CollapsibleTrigger.vue:25 read the empty string at its own first render and is never invalidated. Probe on AccordionChromatic 'Uncontrolled (Single closed)': before any interaction all four triggers = ["","","",""] while the four regions already carry ids reka-collapsible-content-v-1/3/5/7; after ONE click on trigger 0 the root re-render repopulates all four (`reka-collapsible-content-v-1|true`, `…-3|false`, …). So the relationship an AT needs is absent exactly in the state a page loads in, and present after the first toggle — a class of bug neither axe run catches (aria-controls="" is a valid-but-empty idref list) and no functional test asserts (grep: no `aria-controls` in Accordion/Collapsible tests, either runner). Quarantined as it.fails in the visual file; the plain Collapsible has the same bug, measured in Chromium (2026-08-20, throwaway probe): `<CollapsibleRoot><CollapsibleTrigger/><CollapsibleContent/>` renders aria-controls="" at rest while the content already has id reka-collapsible-content-v-0, one click fills it; defaultOpen=true is also empty at rest. Upstream v2 @ b32f255 (2026-08-13) carries the identical three lines, so it is not fixed there. UPSTREAM HISTORY (gh, 2026-08-20): known to the maintainer and dropped. Issue unovue/reka-ui#2521 (2026-03-16, 'VoiceOver does not announce expanded/collapsed') led zernonia to open PR #2522 the same day — 'fix(Collapsible): make contentId reactive to fix VoiceOver aria-controls' — whose body states the exact diagnosis ('On initial render aria-controls="" (empty)') and whose diff is the Ref<string> fix across the same three files. The reporter then found their VoiceOver settings were the cause of the *announcement* symptom, the issue closed as user error (2026-03-18), and the PR was closed unmerged the next day. No open issue names the empty aria-controls itself; the related open work (#2597/#2774/#2882/#2883) is the opposite shape — triggers that keep an aria-controls pointing at UNMOUNTED popup content. NOT A BROWSER-MODE WIN, measured: the same _Collapsible.vue fixture mounted under jsdom (VTU mount, defaultOpen) reads aria-controls="" at rest, content id reka-collapsible-content-v-0, and the filled id after trigger('click') — identical to Chromium, because Vue's render order is the environment's, not the DOM's. jsdom had this attribute empty in every Accordion/Collapsible test since they were written; grep: zero aria-controls assertions in either runner's Accordion or Collapsible tests before this. What surfaced it was the visual-sheet WORKFLOW — render the story as a page loads, inspect BEFORE any interaction (the click is the one action that repairs the attribute), and write exact assertions for the relations a screenshot cannot show — plus axe being structurally blind to valid-but-empty ARIA in both runners. Book it as a workflow finding, the way cleanup() teardown coverage is booked as the harness's, not Chromium's.

The trailing comma is the React-Aria/melt convention for a segment name that is CONCATENATED with the field label via aria-labelledby — reka kept the comma and dropped the concatenation.
