FIXTURE BUG exposed by WebKit: `DateField`/`TimeField` tests pass `locale: 'en-UK'`, which is not a valid BCP 47 tag (the region is GB). V8 and SpiderMonkey (ICU) alias UK→GB, so `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-UK').resolvedOptions().locale` is `en-GB` and the field renders `dd/mm/yyyy` with no day period; JavaScriptCore resolves it to `en` (measured: `{resolved: 'en', hour12: true, order: month,day,year,hour,minute,dayPeriod}`) — so `changes segment positioning based on locale` (`'mm'` where `'dd'` expected), `doesnt show the day period for locales that don't use them` (DateField and TimeField) fail on WebKit, macOS and Linux alike. The tests have asserted an engine's alias table since jsdom. Fix is one character in each fixture (`en-GB`); recorded, not patched (non-test source rule does not apply, but the port's verbatim-name rule does — the test bodies stay as ported).

ENGINE DIFFERENCE: the six PinInput paste tests and two TagsInput delimiter-paste tests synthesize `new ClipboardEvent('paste', { clipboardData })` with a script-built `DataTransfer`. Chromium and WebKit deliver the data (`getData('text/plain') === 'test'`); Firefox delivers a non-null `clipboardData` whose `getData` returns `''` (measured, macOS and Linux) — a script-constructed DataTransfer is emptied when it crosses into a ClipboardEvent. So eight tests that pass on Chromium exercise an empty paste on Firefox: boxes stay `['', '', '', '', '']`, no `complete` emit, no tags. Nothing in the component is wrong; the synthetic paste is Chromium/WebKit-only. A real paste (`userEvent.paste` after writing the clipboard) would be the engine-neutral gesture; not attempted here.

ENGINE DIFFERENCE that unmasks a fixture accident: `ColorArea` 'thumb gains focus when dragging starts' dispatches a synthetic `pointerdown` with `pointerId: 1` and the component calls `setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)`. In Chromium and WebKit the real mouse IS pointer 1 (measured `pointerId` on a real hover: chromium 1, webkit 1, firefox 0), so the capture call silently succeeds and the handler goes on to focus the thumb. In Firefox the mouse is pointer 0, pointer 1 never existed, `setPointerCapture(1)` throws `NotFoundError: Invalid pointer id`, the handler aborts before `thumbRef.focus()`, and the test fails with an unhandled error on top. AGENTS.md's 'you cannot fake a pointerId' gotcha said Chrome throws; it does not when the faked id happens to be the mouse's. The synthetic event passes on two engines by coincidence of id numbering.

SERIALIZATION DIFFERENCE: `innerHTML` attribute order is engine-specific when `style` is written through the CSSOM. ScrollArea's five `toMatchSnapshot` tests fail on Firefox and Tree's on Firefox and WebKit, and a token diff shows zero differing attributes — only order: Chromium serializes `tabindex="0" style="overflow: hidden scroll; …"`, Firefox `style="…" tabindex="0"`; Tree's `<ul>` is `role="tree" style="outline: none;"` in Chromium and `style role` in Firefox/WebKit, and every `<li>` moves `style="margin-left: 1rem;"` ahead of the `aria-*` attributes. The `.snap` files are Chromium baselines; they are not portable across engines any more than across fonts (#snapshots-real-geometry). Expected-fail on the other engines rather than normalized — a serializer that sorts attributes would hide the one thing the snapshot exists to pin.

PLATFORM TRUTH (macOS only): a real click on a `<button>` or `<a href>` does not focus it in WebKit on macOS (measured: `activeElement` stays BODY after `locator.click()` on both; on Linux WebKit focuses both, like Chromium and Firefox everywhere). NavigationMenu's 'after pressing down key' pair therefore fails on darwin WebKit — ArrowDown goes to BODY because the trigger was never focused by the click that opened the menu — and passes in the Linux container. Recorded as a `darwin`-scoped expectation; it is the browser implementing the OS convention, not a component or harness bug.

PLATFORM TRUTH (macOS only): sequential focus in WebKit on macOS skips links and buttons unless the OS 'full keyboard access' setting is on (measured Tab path from a button: `BUTTON → INPUT → BODY` on darwin, `BUTTON → A → BUTTON → INPUT` on Linux; Firefox tabs to both on both platforms). So NavigationMenu 'after pressing tab → should focus on the first item' and DatePicker 'navigates the segments using tab' (Tab from the last segment must land on the trigger button) fail on darwin WebKit and pass on Linux WebKit. `darwin`-scoped expectations.

ENGINE DIFFERENCE, both platforms: in DatePicker, ArrowRight from the last segment focuses the trigger button on every engine, but a further ArrowRight on the focused trigger moves focus BACK to the timeZoneName segment in WebKit (measured path `… timeZoneName → trigger → timeZoneName`; Chromium and Firefox stay on the trigger). 'navigates segments using the arrow keys' asserts the trigger keeps focus and fails on WebKit. Mechanism not traced — it is either the field's keydown handler reading a stale focused-segment index under WebKit's focus event order, or WebKit's own key handling on a focused button. [mechanism unverified]

A QUARANTINED BUG THAT IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC: `HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts#pending-focus-reopens` (it.fails: a real focus, touch-open, touch-close leaves the trigger reopened by the pending focus timer) does NOT reproduce on WebKit — the test passes, which under `it.fails` reads as 'Expect test to fail'. Recorded as a `passes` expectation so the WebKit run requires it green; the day it fails on WebKit too, the row goes stale and says so. Mechanism not traced. [unverified]

NONDETERMINISTIC ON FIREFOX AND WEBKIT: `Drawer.snap.browser.test.ts` reads `--drawer-snap-point-offset` synchronously after `click` + three `nextTick`s. On Chromium all 6 pass every time. On WebKit (macOS and Linux) the same three tests fail in every isolated run (`0px` where `448px` expected: REOPEN after close, REOPEN after snap transition + close, snap-to-snap release) — and in one whole-corpus run under CPU load the fourth, 'on initial open', failed as well. On Firefox two of the three fail per run but WHICH two changes run to run (5 runs: 4 distinct pairs), and the Linux container failed 'on initial open' instead. Both engines are therefore marked `skip` for all four offset-write tests rather than pinned to a verdict. The same open/close/reopen sequence probed in a fresh page writes `448px` synchronously on all three engines, so this is test-order/state-dependent and the root cause (the lazy watcher the test names, or ResizeObserver delivery timing under Gecko/WebKit) is [unverified]. Worth a real look: it is the one file where a non-Chromium engine may be showing the regression the test was written for.

METHOD: the Linux column of the expectations table was measured, not assumed — the repo was copied into the pinned `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble` image (the CI container), `pnpm i --frozen-lockfile`, and the same `--no-file-parallelism` runs were made for firefox and webkit.
